name: pgvector
documentation: VectorStorePort over PostgreSQL's pgvector extension, through the existing DatabasePort. No new daemon: a project that already runs PostgreSQL adds one extension. Every collection is one table (hkm_vec_<name>) with a vector(N) column, a jsonb payload, an optional HNSW index and a GIN index on the payload.
//no-routes: A vector search is a primitive for other modules, not an endpoint. An unauthenticated search route would be a query oracle over whatever was embedded — which is usually the private text the application holds — so the capability is a port and the application decides who may ask.
//kernel-floor: ^1.20.0: VectorStorePort and EmbeddingPort first appear in the release after 1.19.0. The floor is set to that release; it was not established by `git tag --contains` because the ports are not yet tagged.
//requires-database-management: The store needs a DatabasePort bound to PostgreSQL with the `vector` extension created. database.management is declared so the module joins the dependency graph of any route that asks for vector.store; the binding is a PostgreSQL connection, checked at first use (through DriverAware when the adapter has it).
